\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أقلع} (aqlaʿa)}{أقلع (aqlaʿa)}]{\ar{أقلع} (aqlaʿa) — to lift off; to take off (of a plane)}

\label{lesson:AR-C424-aqlaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for boarding, then the Arabic for a runway.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أقلع}}
\textbf{\ar{أقلع}} — \emph{aqlaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to lift off; to take off (of a plane)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أقلعت} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{متأخرة} \ar{بسبب} \ar{الضباب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aqlaʿat ar-riḥla mutaʾakhkhira bi-sabab aḍ-ḍabāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flight took off late because of the fog.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقلع}, \emph{yuqliʿ}.

With \emph{ʿan} it means to give up a habit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أقلع}} (\emph{aqlaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-l-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to pull up, to uproot\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Aqlaʿa} is Form IV; the same root gives \emph{qilʿ}, usually glossed as the sail of a ship.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqlaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqlaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqlaʿat ar-riḥla mutaʾakhkhira bi-sabab aḍ-ḍabāb.} — The flight took off late because of the fog.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for boarding, then the Arabic for a runway, then say \emph{aqlaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أقلع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To lift off; to take off (of a plane)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{هبط} (habaṭa)}{هبط (habaṭa)}]{\ar{هبط} (habaṭa) — to land; to go down}

\label{lesson:AR-C424-habata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a runway, then the Arabic for to lift off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{هبط}}
\textbf{\ar{هبط}} — \emph{habaṭa} — \textquotedblleft{}to land; to go down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هبطت} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{في} \ar{مطار} \ar{صغير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{habaṭat ar-riḥla fī maṭār ṣaghīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flight landed at a small airport.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يهبط}, \emph{yahbiṭ}.

Lane gives the present both as \emph{yahbiṭu} and \emph{yahbuṭu}; \emph{hubūṭ} is a landing.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{هبط}} (\emph{habaṭa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-b-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to descend, to go down\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the plain verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{habaṭa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{habaṭa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{habaṭat ar-riḥla fī maṭār ṣaghīr.} — The flight landed at a small airport.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a runway, then the Arabic for to lift off, then say \emph{habaṭa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{هبط} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To land; to go down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إقلاع} (iqlāʿ)}{إقلاع (iqlāʿ)}]{\ar{إقلاع} (iqlāʿ) — takeoff}

\label{lesson:AR-C424-iqla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to lift off, then the Arabic for to land.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إقلاع}}
\textbf{\ar{إقلاع}} — \emph{iqlāʿ} — \textquotedblleft{}takeoff\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{جلس} \ar{المسافرون} \ar{في} \ar{مقاعدهم} \ar{قبل} \ar{الإقلاع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jalasa al-musāfirūn fī maqāʿidihim qabla al-iqlāʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The passengers sat in their seats before takeoff.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إقلاع}} (\emph{iqlāʿ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-l-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to pull up, to uproot\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the verbal noun of Form IV \emph{aqlaʿa}, \textquotedblleft{}to take off\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iqlāʿ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iqlāʿ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalasa al-musāfirūn fī maqāʿidihim qabla al-iqlāʿ.} — The passengers sat in their seats before takeoff.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to lift off, then the Arabic for to land, then say \emph{iqlāʿ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{إقلاع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Takeoff\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حزام} \ar{أمان} (ḥizām amān)}{حزام أمان (ḥizām amān)}]{\ar{حزام} \ar{أمان} (ḥizām amān) — a seat belt}

\label{lesson:AR-C424-hizam-aman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to land, then the Arabic for takeoff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حزام} \ar{أمان}}
\textbf{\ar{حزام} \ar{أمان}} — \emph{ḥizām amān} — \textquotedblleft{}a seat belt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ربط} \ar{الطفل} \ar{حزام} \ar{الأمان}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rabaṭa aṭ-ṭifl ḥizām al-amān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child fastened the seat belt.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حزام} \ar{أمان}} (\emph{ḥizām amān}) is built from two native Arabic words: \emph{ḥizām}, \textquotedblleft{}a belt\textquotedblright{}, on the root \emph{ḥ-z-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to bind, to tie up\textquotedblright{} (Lane), and \emph{amān}, \textquotedblleft{}safety\textquotedblright{}, on the root \emph{ʾ-m-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be safe\textquotedblright{} (Lane): a belt of safety.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥizām amān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥizām amān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rabaṭa aṭ-ṭifl ḥizām al-amān.} — The child fastened the seat belt.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to land, then the Arabic for takeoff, then say \emph{ḥizām amān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حزام} \ar{أمان} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A seat belt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طاقم} (ṭāqam)}{طاقم (ṭāqam)}]{\ar{طاقم} (ṭāqam) — a crew; a set}

\label{lesson:AR-C424-taqam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for takeoff, then the Arabic for a seat belt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طاقم}}
\textbf{\ar{طاقم}} — \emph{ṭāqam} — \textquotedblleft{}a crew; a set\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{طاقم} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{لطيفا} \ar{جدا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna ṭāqam ar-riḥla laṭīfan jiddan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flight crew was very kind.
\end{quote}

It also names a matching set: \emph{ṭāqam shāy}, a tea set.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طاقم}} (\emph{ṭāqam}) was borrowed from Ottoman Turkish (EtymDB), where \emph{takım} means a set or a team.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭāqam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna ṭāqam ar-riḥla laṭīfan jiddan.} — The flight crew was very kind.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for takeoff, then the Arabic for a seat belt, then say \emph{ṭāqam} again
\end{itemize}
